edges.description: Supplying wild-type NDUFC2 to the patients' own cells restores assembly, which is the demonstration that the variants rather than something else in those genomes cause the stall.
edges.limitations: The rescue is partial in both lines and neither reaches control levels of assembled complex I, and the authors work through why: complex I is thought to assemble within 24 hours and the induction ran for 72, so time is not the limitation, but the mutant protein or the aberrant subassemblies already present may interfere. The system is a cultured fibroblast, so it says nothing about brain; the third patient could not be tested at all for lack of material; and doxycycline-driven expression is non-physiological in level and timing.

edges.description: Complexome profiling is what resolves an assembly defect into a module-level map. It showed the loss of NDUFC2's associating subunits in the ND1 and ND2 modules, the independent survival of the ND4 module, and the complete absence of ND5 and N module intermediates.
edges.limitations: Cultured fibroblasts, not the affected tissue, and two patients. The readout is abundance across a gradient rather than a direct measurement of assembly order, so the assembly sequence is inferred by comparing the observed intermediates against a published model. The scaffold interpretation the authors draw from it is offered as a possibility rather than a conclusion.

nodes.description: The tissue lesion that defines Leigh syndrome, and it is present in all three children. Imaging showed bilateral symmetrical high T2 signal in the thalami, substantia nigra and medulla in the first patient, in the basal ganglia and lentiform nuclei in her brother, and in the thalami, basal ganglia and brainstem in the third. The first patient also had corticospinal-tract signal change with white matter volume loss and periventricular leukomalacia; the second had a Dandy-Walker malformation with partial corpus callosum agenesis, which is a malformation rather than a degenerative lesion and is recorded as its own phenotype.

nodes.description: Two damaged copies of NDUFC2. Two alleles are known and each is homozygous in one family. The Saudi siblings carry c.346_*7del, a 22-nucleotide deletion that removes the stop codon and replaces the last four residues with a 21-residue extension, p.(His116_Arg119delins21). The Moroccan boy carries c.173A>T, p.(His58Leu), at a histidine conserved across species, with every in silico predictor calling it damaging. Neither allele class is present homozygously in population databases: gnomAD contains no homozygous loss-of-function NDUFC2 variant at all.

nodes.description: Losing NDUFC2 takes its neighbours with it. Complexome profiling of both index patients shows concurrent loss of the subunits NDUFC2 associates with, in the ND1 and ND2 modules. The negative results are as informative as the positive ones: neither an ND5 nor an N module intermediate was found at all, while the distal ND4 module was still detected - so the distal membrane module assembles independently while the two proximal ones do not. The authors read this as NDUFC2 possibly acting as a scaffold for ND1 module formation.

nodes.description: Complex I does not work alone: it associates with complexes III and IV into supercomplexes, and those are lost too. Blue native electrophoresis of digitonin-solubilised patient mitochondria shows a dramatic deficiency of the complex I-containing supercomplexes. This is a consequence of having no holoenzyme to incorporate rather than a separate lesion, but it is worth recording as its own node because it is what the respiratory measurements are made against.

nodes.description: NDUFC2 is a membrane protein of the proton-pumping arm, assigned to the ND2 module, facing the intermembrane space, and in contact with twelve other subunits - NDUFA8 in the ND1 module, five subunits of its own ND2 module, and five of the ND4 module. That is an unusual amount of connectivity for a small accessory subunit and is the structural reason a defect in it is an assembly defect rather than a catalytic one. Complexome profiling of patient fibroblasts confirms the loss of NDUFC2 itself.

nodes.description: Assembly does not fail from the start - it gets part-way and stops. The Q module forms successfully, and the process then halts because the ND1 subunit is not incorporated into the inner membrane, leaving aberrant intermediates rather than holoenzyme. In one patient's fibroblasts no fully assembled complex I was detectable at all; in the other it was greatly decreased. All other oxidative phosphorylation complexes were unaffected, which is what makes the deficiency isolated.
